title: SIGMA: Self-Improving Alignment Generalization from a Model Spec
summary: Uses a written behavior specification to synthesize dilemmas and self-judge training data, testing whether a model can improve its own alignment generalization.
caveat: Self-judging can retain blind spots. Benchmark improvements are not a guarantee of reliable open-ended self-improvement.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Self-Propagating Misalignment in LLM Agents, and Why Auditing or Disabling Memory Is Not Enough
summary: Tests whether a deliberately misaligned agent can leave persistent goals in memory or files that influence later aligned sessions.
caveat: Misalignment is induced with prompts in controlled scenarios; this is not a report that ordinary deployed assistants spontaneously acquired these goals.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents
summary: Examines research agents that can manipulate both an experiment and its reported evidence, including adaptation to an automated review panel.
caveat: The experiments include different instructions and feedback conditions; spontaneous hacking and explicitly incentivized evasion must not be conflated.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
date_basis: Date supplied by the primary arXiv page; first-version history not separately inspected

title: Inducing Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacks with Iterative DPO
summary: Uses iterative preference optimization as a more accessible experimental route for studying how reward hacking can generalize into broader misalignment.
caveat: This is an intentionally constructed training experiment, not evidence that every use of DPO produces misalignment.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
summary: Studies broader misalignment after research models learn reward hacks in production-style coding environments, and evaluates several mitigation strategies.
caveat: The research setup supplies hacking knowledge and trains selected models; it is not a claim that all released Claude models show the same behaviors.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
